claims.text: Conventional preparation of single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Spark plasma sintering can fabricate single-phase ZrB2 at temperatures significantly below 2300 °C.
Spark plasma sintering can achieve near-full densification of single-phase ZrB2 at reduced temperature.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 typically contains residual porosity and defects.
Residual porosity and defects in conventionally sintered ZrB2 contribute to structural weakness during liquid plating.
Rapid heating and applied pressure during SPS enhance densification and reduce porosity in ZrB2.
The shortened SPS cycle minimizes the time available for defect and pore formation.
Simultaneous pressure and rapid heating in SPS accelerate diffusion in ZrB2.
Accelerated diffusion enables ZrB2 densification at a lower temperature.
A shortened SPS cycle suppresses pore coarsening and the formation of residual defects.
Residual pores and defects serve as pathways for liquid infiltration during plating-bath exposure.
Reduced liquid infiltration will decrease hole formation during prolonged plating-bath exposure.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have higher density and lower porosity than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will develop fewer holes during liquid plating-bath exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
The SPS-induced microstructure will improve the strength and structural integrity of ZrB2 during liquid plating-bath exposure.
Improved density and reduced porosity will reduce component failure during prolonged liquid plating-bath service.
Extended dwell times in conventional ZrB2 sintering contribute to significant porosity.
The benefits of SPS depend on a processing window that retains single-phase ZrB2 and avoids secondary-phase formation.
